chapter: Banjo career, Armstrong and the Liberty Bell
title: Tony Jackson, the solo pianist, and drummer Bruno Joseph
summary: Vincent remembers Tony Jackson as a well-known solo piano player who did not play with bands. He then describes drummer Bruno Joseph, who died after drinking bad corn whiskey.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Ask him about Tony Jackson. He wanted to tell us about Tony Jackson.

So he wanted to tell us about Tony Jackson. Tony Jackson? Well, Tony Jackson, that fellow was a, you know, this cabinet player. He used to play on hold, you know, all the time. He was a piano player. He used to say he was a morphedizer, you know. And the other part of it too, Bunnell. Both of them was good. But then Bunnell used to high sometimes with piano and banjo. Piano and guitar. Like that, you know. In them little, what do you call them, little beer parties, you know. Just two pieces. I played with them twice at Thomas Benton's place, you know. But them brothers was good. They had one man with piano by their self, you know, those guys like that. And I don't remember Tony Jackson playing with no band, you know. This was a well-known piano player. And then, uh, I'll tell you about little, uh, Bruno Joseph, the drummer. Little Crippie Patti. He's good. He's supposed to be in Dallas. He'll be better here for him no more. I'll be, I don't be there, because he's kind of fat. If he's living, he might be out in California or Chicago or New York somewhere. He's a good little drummer. He's better with a drummer too. Joseph's Joseph. He died. He's a little bit of an insect. And he died. And his mother said, somebody poisoned him. I couldn't drink that stuff with six, I couldn't drink a spoon for it. And two cocoa bottles. That stuff you should make sure, and I had to stop. But bones are standing. And that's what Jersey's tried to do. Trying to burn all these eyes out. He went blind. All his mouth was burnt. Killed it. They call it shimmy, that whiskey. Corn whiskey.
